extracted.intended_audience: hospital quality officers, hospital administrators, measure developers, policymakers, and other stakeholders involved in CMS hospital quality measurement and Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program
extracted.subtask_description: Specifications and implementation guidance for the Hospital 30-Day, All-Cause, Risk-Standardized Readmission Rate Following Sepsis Hospitalization measure proposed for use in the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program, including numerator/denominator definitions, risk adjustment, reliability, data sources, reporting, and payment implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Sepsis Readmission measure
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Sepsis Readmission measure is to improve patient outcomes by providing patients, physicians, hospitals, and policymakers with important information about hospital-level unplanned readmission rates following hospitalization for sepsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measure would encourage hospitals to improve patient safety and the quality of care provided across the care continuum by tracking hospital-level rates of sepsis readmission, promote adherence to evidence-based practices (including standardized clinical protocols, implementation of targeted post-discharge interventions, and appropriate discharge planning), and give consumers meaningful insights into the quality of care received by Medicare patients. The measure aligns with CMS' Meaningful Measures 2.0 priority area of 'Seamless Care Coordination.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Population and inclusion criteria (age, payer, diagnosis, setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes Medicare Fee-for-Service or Medicare Advantage beneficiaries aged 65 years and older who were discharged from a non-federal short-term acute care hospital with a principal diagnosis of sepsis (including post-procedural sepsis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patients must have been enrolled in Medicare FFS or MA during the index admission and for the 12 months prior to the date of admission; discharged alive from a non-federal short-term acute care hospital; and not transferred to another acute care facility. The measure has been specified to include both Medicare Fee-for-Service and Medicare Advantage beneficiaries to ensure consistent measurement across Medicare beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator: 30-day all-cause readmission definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator is Medicare FFS or MA beneficiaries aged 65+ with a principal diagnosis of sepsis at index discharge who were readmitted to an acute care hospital for any cause within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only an unplanned inpatient admission to a short-term acute care hospital can qualify as a readmission. Planned readmissions are not included in the numerator. For details of measure methodology, see the methodology report on QualityNet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator definition and index admission eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator includes Medicare FFS or MA beneficiaries aged 65+ hospitalized at non-federal short-term acute care hospitals who are discharged alive following a principal hospital discharge diagnosis of sepsis and with continuous 12-month Medicare enrollment prior to the index hospitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index admissions excluded include: (1) admissions where patient leaves AMA; (2) admissions for patients without at least 30 days post-discharge enrollment in Medicare FFS or MA; (3) admissions resulting in discharge to hospice; (4) sepsis admissions captured in the pneumonia readmission measure; and (5) sepsis admissions within 30 days of an eligible sepsis index admission (because they are considered readmissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of transfers and hospice/AMA and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude patients transferred to another acute care facility, discharges to hospice, and admissions where patients left against medical advice from measure eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers excluded because the index hospital may not be the appropriate entity for attribution; hospice discharges excluded because readmission may not be a meaningful outcome for hospice patients; AMA excluded because providers may not have the opportunity to deliver full care and prepare the patient for discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of overlap with pneumonia readmission measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude sepsis admissions that are captured in the pneumonia readmission measure to avoid overlap between measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents double-counting index admissions across condition-specific readmission measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment variables (what to adjust for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure includes risk adjustments for patient factors such as age, comorbid diseases, indicators of patient frailty, aggressiveness of infectious organism (bacteria, virus, or fungus), transplant recipient indicator, and clinical markers of severe sepsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These variables are included because they are clinically relevant and related to the outcome. For each patient, risk adjustment variables are obtained from inpatient, outpatient, and physician Medicare administrative claims data extending up to 12 months prior to the index hospitalization, and secondary diagnoses documented as present on admission during the index hospitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment exclusions (do not adjust for in-hospital complications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjustment does not include complications that arise during the course of the index hospitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complications that arise during the index hospitalization reflect the quality of care delivered and fall within the causal pathway rather than patient risk, and therefore are excluded from risk adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment data sources and time window
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjustment variables are obtained from Medicare administrative claims (Part A and Part B claims, hospital-submitted MA claims, and MA encounter data) extending up to 12 months prior to the index hospitalization, and POA secondary diagnoses during the index hospitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims-based data are used because they are nationally scalable, consistently available, and minimize provider reporting burden while enabling standardized comparisons across hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of hospital-level 30-day Risk-Standardized Readmission Rate (RSRR)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSRR is calculated as the ratio of the number of predicted readmissions based on the hospital's performance with its observed case mix to the number of expected readmissions based on the average national level of performance with that hospital's case mix, multiplied by the national observed readmission rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the same measure calculation methodology as the current measures in the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program; see methodology report for additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess Readmission Ratio and statistical modeling approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The excess readmission ratio is calculated using hierarchical logistic regression producing an adjusted actual (predicted) number and an expected number, with the ratio comparing a hospital's adjusted actual readmissions to the expected number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hierarchical logistic regression method adjusts for variation across hospitals in patient sickness at admission and variation in patient counts to reveal differences in quality. Hospitals with more adjusted actual readmissions than expected will have an excess readmission ratio greater than one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability testing methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability testing employed standard statistical approaches, specifically split-half (split-sample) reliability, to assess whether observed differences in hospital readmission rates reflect true quality differences rather than random variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability was estimated at both the measure score and accountable-entity levels using two years of data (Jan 1, 2022 – Dec 31, 2023). Testing included hospitals with minimum case thresholds of ≥2 and ≥25 (the proposed threshold for public reporting), and accountable-entity-level reliability was assessed across hospital volume deciles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reliability threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure reliability should meet the minimum standard set by the Partnership for Quality Measurement (>= 0.60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split-half reliability results indicate the measure is sufficiently reliable for distinguishing between high- and low-performing hospitals when meeting this threshold. At the accountable-entity level, 69 percent of entities met the ≥0.60 threshold for hospitals with ≥25 cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum sample size threshold for public reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed threshold for public reporting is hospitals with at least 25 eligible discharges for the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliability analyses were reported for hospitals with ≥2 cases and ≥25 cases; the ≥25 threshold is proposed for public reporting to ensure sufficient reliability and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of coding variability and post-discharge mortality as bias sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses examined coding variability (e.g., use of sepsis code A41.9) and post-discharge mortality within 30 days as potential sources of bias in entity-level performance scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses found no correlation between hospital-level use of sepsis code A41.9 and readmission or mortality risk, and no correlation between post-discharge mortality and readmission risk at the hospital level. Post-discharge mortality was stable up to 30 days. CMS will conduct ongoing monitoring and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure endorsement and PRMR review criteria and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure underwent the Pre-Rulemaking Measure Review (PRMR) process and endorsement review; PRMR Hospital Committee voting and Recommendation Group inputs inform adoption decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRMR Hospital Review (Jan 12–13, 2026) resulted in 65% recommending adoption (consensus not reached); concerns raised included adoption into HRRP, methodological issues, and need for sepsis definition consistency. The Cost and Efficiency Recommendation Group later endorsed the measure (84% vote) in Fall 2025 cycle without conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation approach and 'early look' reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to adopt the Sepsis Readmission measure directly into the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program with a phased approach that includes 'early look' confidential reports prior to using the measure for payment adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early look reports for FY 2028 (applicable period July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2026) would include sepsis readmission rates and estimated HRRP payment adjustments but would not be publicly reported or used for payment; measure use for payment adjustment is proposed beginning FY 2029 (applicable period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027). CMS considered but did not adopt initial placement in Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data submission and requirement for hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Sepsis Readmission measure uses CMS administrative data; hospitals are not required to submit additional data to calculate the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data sources include Medicare FFS Part A and B claims, hospital-submitted Medicare Advantage claims, and Medicare Advantage Organization-submitted encounter data. FY 2026 rule finalized use of 2 years of claims data for readmission measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries for consistent measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Including Medicare Advantage beneficiaries in CMS hospital outcome measures to ensure hospital quality is measured consistently across all Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusion is consistent with prior HRRP policy changes (FY 2026 final rule) to integrate MA beneficiaries into HRRP cohorts beginning FY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting venues and cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: If finalized, CMS would publicly report readmission rates annually for applicable conditions for each hospital on the Compare tool (medicare.gov care-compare) and on the Provider Data Catalog (data.cms.gov/provider-data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reporting is codified at §412.154(f). Early look reports would be confidential and not publicly reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment adjustment calculation and program methodology references
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of sepsis readmissions in aggregate payments for excess readmissions affects the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program payment adjustment factor, calculated per the formula codified at §412.152 and methodology at §412.154(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate payments for excess readmissions include aggregate base operating DRG payments for excess readmissions associated with sepsis. The estimated average payment reduction per penalized hospital when including the Sepsis Readmission measure increased by approximately $63,500 in CMS analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of subgroup impacts and ongoing measure maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing evaluation of measure performance characteristics including hospital-level reliability, year-over-year stability, and subgroup impacts (e.g., rural/low-volume hospitals) as part of routine measure maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will monitor for unintended consequences, coding practice impacts, and the need for alignment of sepsis definitions across measures and payers; ongoing monitoring and maintenance are part of routine operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on sepsis definition consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee emphasized need for greater consistency in sepsis definitions across measures and payors, with many urging alignment with Sepsis-3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS noted differing definitions reflect tradeoffs between sensitivity and specificity; literature shows common problems with sepsis diagnoses relate to under-coding. CMS conducted analyses of coding practices and found no evidence that coding variability drove performance scores.
